title: The General Ledger
description: Understand where accounting transactions are organized.
html:
What is the general ledger?

The general ledger is the collection of all accounts used by a business.

After transactions are recorded in the journal, the amounts are posted into the appropriate ledger accounts.

Think of it this way

The journal records transactions in date order.

The general ledger organizes those transactions by account.

Example

Suppose a company has these transactions:

  • Owner invests $10,000 cash.
  • Company pays $2,000 cash for equipment.
  • Company earns $1,500 cash revenue.

Cash

Owner investment + $10,000
Equipment purchase - $2,000
Revenue received + $1,500
Ending Balance: $9,500

Equipment

Equipment purchase + $2,000
Ending Balance: $2,000

Revenue

Revenue earned + $1,500
Ending Balance: $1,500

Why the ledger matters

  • It shows the balance of each account.
  • It groups transactions by account.
  • It helps prepare the trial balance.
  • It helps accountants find and review transactions.

quiz.prompt: What is the main purpose of the general ledger?
quiz.explanation: The general ledger organizes financial activity by account and shows each account's balance.
